1.title: Cost-Optimized Storage
1.text: Welcome to Module eleven: Cost-Optimized Storage. This module covers task statement four point one, the first task of Domain four, Design Cost-Optimized Architectures, which carries twenty percent of the exam. You will use the cost tools, choose the cheapest S three class and lifecycle for an access pattern, control block and file storage costs, plan backups, and move data cheaply. The exam describes a bill and a pattern, and asks for the cheapest fit.

1.title: What You Will Learn
1.text: By the end of this module you will be able to do five things. Use Cost Explorer, Budgets, Cost and Usage Reports, tags and consolidated billing. Choose the cheapest S three storage class and lifecycle for an access pattern. Control E B S, E F S and F S x costs. Pick backup and archival strategies with sensible retention. And choose the lowest-cost way to move data into A W S storage.

1.title: Case Check-In: Lantern and Loom Trims the Storage Bill
1.text: The storage bill at Lantern and Loom has tripled. Product images have reached forty terabytes, and most are rarely viewed. Nightly backups must be kept for seven years. Oversized and forgotten E B S volumes pile up. And partners pull large data sets and upload by S F T P. Your job is to find and fix the waste.

1.title: Cost Management Tools
1.text: Three tools show and control cost. A W S Cost Explorer lets you visualize and analyze cost and usage: filter, group, see thirteen months of history, forecast ahead, and get savings recommendations. A W S Budgets sets limits for cost, usage, Reserved Instance and Savings Plans, and alerts you by email or S N S when actual or forecast spend crosses a threshold; it can also run budget actions. The Cost and Usage Report is the most detailed cost data, delivered to S three by hour, day or month, with tags, and you can query it with Athena. All three read the same underlying billing data. Exam tip: seeing costs is Cost Explorer; getting warned is Budgets; line-item detail is the Cost and Usage Report.

1.title: Tags, Accounts and Consolidated Billing
1.text: A cost allocation tag is a key and value label that groups costs by project, team or application. There are two kinds: A W S-generated and user-defined, and you must activate them in the Billing console first. Active tags appear in Cost Explorer and the Cost and Usage Report, after up to twenty-four hours. Consolidated billing in A W S Organizations gives one bill, combines usage for volume discounts, shares Reserved Instance and Savings Plans discounts, and costs nothing extra. Use separate accounts per workload to track cost. Exam tip: cost by team or project means activated tags; lower rates across accounts means consolidated billing.

1.title: S3 Storage Classes
1.text: S three storage classes step down in price and up in retrieval cost. S three Standard is for frequent access, with no minimum duration. Intelligent-Tiering suits unknown or changing patterns. Standard-I A is for monthly access, with a thirty-day minimum and a retrieval fee. One Zone-I A is for re-creatable data in one zone. Glacier Instant Retrieval is for quarterly access in milliseconds, with a ninety-day minimum. Glacier Flexible Retrieval is for minutes to hours, also ninety days. And Glacier Deep Archive is for data read less than once a year, with a one hundred eighty-day minimum. The figure shows the seven steps. Exam tip: the colder the class, the cheaper the storage and the costlier the retrieval.

1.title: S3 Intelligent-Tiering and Lifecycle Rules
1.text: Two approaches reduce cost over time. Intelligent-Tiering moves objects between tiers by access: Infrequent after thirty days, and Archive Instant after ninety days. There are no retrieval fees, only a small monitoring fee, so it suits unknown or changing access. Lifecycle rules transition objects after a set age and expire them, for existing and new objects, which suits access that declines predictably. Objects under one hundred twenty-eight kilobytes are not tiered, and the infrequent access classes bill a one hundred twenty-eight kilobyte minimum. Deleting early still bills the minimum duration. Exam tip: predictable aging means lifecycle rules; unpredictable access means Intelligent-Tiering.

1.title: S3 Glacier Retrieval and Archiving
1.text: Glacier classes differ in how you get data back. Glacier Instant Retrieval gives millisecond, direct reads. Glacier Flexible Retrieval needs a restore first: Expedited takes one to five minutes, Standard takes three to five hours, and Bulk takes five to twelve hours. Glacier Deep Archive also needs a restore: Standard within twelve hours, and Bulk within forty-eight hours. Bulk is the cheapest way to restore, and it is free for Flexible Retrieval. Batch Operations restores many objects in one request. Objects stay in S three; the old separate Glacier service is not used for these. Exam tip: cheapest archive when hours are fine means Deep Archive with Bulk retrieval.

1.title: S3 Cost Levers
1.text: Several S three settings reduce cost. With Requester Pays, the requester pays for requests and the data download, the owner pays for storage, and requests must be authenticated. Fewer, larger uploads cost less in requests than many tiny ones, and multipart upload suits big files. Expire incomplete multipart uploads and old versions with lifecycle rules. S three Storage Lens shows usage across the organization and recommends savings. Storage Class Analysis advises when to move data to Standard-I A. Data into S three is free; the main fees are storage, requests, retrieval and data out. Exam tip: to share data without paying for downloads, use Requester Pays.

1.title: Block Storage Cost: EBS
1.text: For E B S, G P three lets you choose I O P S and throughput apart from size, so it usually beats G P two on cost. H D D volumes, S T one and S C one, are cheapest per gigabyte for throughput or cold data, but they cannot boot. Right-size volumes, and delete unattached ones. Snapshots are incremental, so frequent snapshots store only the changes. Snapshot Archive cuts storage cost by up to seventy-five percent for snapshots kept ninety days or longer. And Data Lifecycle Manager automates snapshot schedules and deletion, at no extra cost. Exam tip: pay only for the performance used: G P three for S S D, and H D D for big sequential data.

2.title: File Storage Cost: EFS and FSx
2.text: For file storage, E F S lifecycle policies move files to Infrequent Access after thirty days by default, and to Archive after ninety days. One Zone file systems cost less, and Elastic throughput charges only for what you use. For F S x for Windows File Server, use H D D storage for shares and home directories, and S S D only when latency matters. Single-A Z costs less than Multi-A Z, and you can scale storage, I O P S and throughput separately. For storage auto scaling, S three and E F S grow and shrink by themselves, while E B S and F S x are resized by you, and you can turn on R D S storage autoscaling for databases. Exam tip: shared files that are rarely read belong in E F S lifecycle to Infrequent Access or Archive.

2.title: Backup and Archival Strategy
2.text: Plan backups to match the recovery point objective, and use incremental backups to keep frequent copies cheap. A W S Backup plans move backups to cold storage and delete them after retention. Keep each copy only as long as the rules require: set retention on automated backups, and delete old manual snapshots. For long-term archives, use S three Glacier classes, optionally with Object Lock. Cross-Region and cross-account copies add storage and transfer cost, so use them only where truly needed. And test restores, not just backups. Exam tip: the cheapest compliant archive is a cold storage class plus a lifecycle that expires it on schedule.

2.title: Moving Data into AWS at Low Cost
2.text: Choose the transfer method by volume and bandwidth. A W S DataSync does online bulk transfer from N F S, S M B and H D F S to S three, E F S and F S x, scheduled and verified. A W S Transfer Family gives managed S F T P, F T P S, F T P and A S two into S three or E F S, with no servers. Storage Gateway gives ongoing hybrid access with a local cache. The Snow Family uses offline devices for very large data or poor bandwidth. And Direct Connect or a V P N gives a steady link for continuing transfers; module fourteen covers them. Compare size divided by bandwidth: if the network would take weeks, ship a device. As of the fifth of November, twenty twenty-six, check which Snow Family devices are available. Exam tip: online and scheduled is DataSync; partners using S F T P is Transfer Family; weeks of network time is Snow.

2.title: Choosing the Cheapest Storage
2.text: Here is the chooser. An unknown access pattern means S three Intelligent-Tiering. Aging, predictable data means a lifecycle to Standard-I A, then Glacier. An archive read once a year, where hours are fine, means Glacier Deep Archive. Re-creatable data means One Zone-I A. A database volume means E B S G P three. Big sequential reads mean E B S S T one. Shared files that are rarely used mean E F S with lifecycle. And partners who should pay for downloads mean Requester Pays. Exam tip: name the access pattern and the retrieval delay you can accept, then pick the tier.

2.title: What the Exam Asks: Cost-Optimized Storage
2.text: Here is what the exam asks. Which S three class or lifecycle fits the access pattern. Which E B S or file option is cheapest for the load. Which backup and retention plan meets the rules. Which transfer service is cheapest for the volume. And which cost tool: Cost Explorer, Budgets, the Cost and Usage Report, tags or consolidated billing. Exam tip: look for the clues: rarely, unknown, hours, weeks, partners and shared.

2.title: Design Check: Lantern and Loom Trims the Storage Bill
2.text: Here is the Design Check. Cover the right column and answer each row yourself. Old product images rarely viewed: a lifecycle from Standard to Standard-I A, then Glacier Instant Retrieval. Unknown access on new uploads: Intelligent-Tiering. Seven-year backups: A W S Backup with a cold-storage lifecycle, or Glacier Deep Archive. Oversized E B S volumes: right-size to G P three, and delete unattached ones. Old E B S snapshots: Snapshot Archive. Partners who pull big data sets: Requester Pays. Partners who upload by S F T P: Transfer Family. And who spent what: activated tags and Cost Explorer.

2.title: Module Recap
2.text: Here is the recap. The tools are Cost Explorer, Budgets, the Cost and Usage Report, activated tags and consolidated billing. In S three, a colder class means cheaper storage and costlier retrieval; use Intelligent-Tiering for unknown access and lifecycle rules for aging. For block and file, use G P three, H D D for throughput, Snapshot Archive and E F S lifecycle. For backup, match frequency to the recovery point and expire on schedule. And to transfer, use DataSync, Transfer Family, or Snow for the very large.

2.title: Practice Question 1
2.text: Question one. New customer uploads at Lantern and Loom have unpredictable access: some are viewed daily, others never again. The team wants lower storage cost without retrieval fees or manual tiering. Which storage class fits? The four options are on the screen. The answer is C: S three Intelligent-Tiering. It moves objects between access tiers automatically, with no retrieval fees. Standard-I A and One Zone-I A charge for retrieval.

2.title: Practice Question 2
2.text: Question two. Lantern and Loom must keep seven years of nightly backups for compliance. The data is almost never read, and a restore may take up to twelve hours. Which option gives the lowest storage cost? The four options are on the screen. The answer is B: S three Glacier Deep Archive, reached through a lifecycle rule. It is the lowest-cost class for data read less than once a year, and a standard restore finishes within twelve hours.

2.title: Practice Question 3
2.text: Question three. Select two. Which two statements about cost allocation tags and consolidated billing are correct? The five options are on the screen. The answers are A and C. Tags appear in Cost Explorer only after activation, and consolidated billing combines usage so volume discounts and Reserved Instance or Savings Plans discounts are shared. Consolidated billing has no extra fee, and reports update through the month.

2.title: Practice Question 4
2.text: Question four. Partners download large data sets from Lantern and Loom's S three bucket every day, and the company wants the partners to pay the request and download charges. What should it configure? The four options are on the screen. The answer is A: Requester Pays on the bucket. The requester pays for requests and data download, while the owner pays for storage, and requests must be authenticated.

2.title: Practice Question 5
2.text: Question five. Partners upload files by S F T P. Lantern and Loom wants no servers to manage, and the files must land in Amazon S three. Which solution fits? The four options are on the screen. The answer is D: A W S Transfer Family with an S F T P server endpoint backed by S three. It is fully managed, so there are no servers to run.

2.title: Answers at a Glance
2.text: Here are all five answers. Question one: C. Question two: B. Question three: A and C. Question four: A. Question five: D. In Module twelve, we cut the cost of compute.
